# Interview Guide

Pitch uses conversation to expose the problem, not to approve a design. Ask only the next question whose answer could materially change the narrative or whether work should exist.

## Lenses

| Lens | Evidence to seek |
|------|------------------|
| Affected people | Who experiences the friction, risk, or missed opportunity |
| Current reality | What happens now, with concrete examples rather than abstractions |
| Consequence | Why the current reality matters and what it costs |
| Desired outcome | Observable change without prescribing the mechanism |
| First rideable journey | Smallest useful end-to-end outcome for a real operator, expressed without designing component layers |
| Constraints | Boundaries that genuinely remove options |
| Unknowns | Uncertainty important enough to affect shaping |

When a user has already supplied a strong answer, preserve it and move to the next gap. When evidence conflicts, name the conflict instead of averaging it away. End once the narrative can be shaped without guessing at the core problem or the first useful journey. Pitch names that journey; shape later makes its entry point, proof, dogfood, learning, and deferrals concrete.
